description:
## Goal

Explain and remove excess work in recursive TransportShape and CallableConstruction
products without guessing whether the defect is product population, re-settlement,
or cycle-detection scans.

## The counts available today are FLOORS, not counts

Product settlement is systematically under-reported, so every number below is a
lower bound. Two settle paths emit nothing:

- `ProductMemo::finish_group` (`pull.rs:458`) inserts N-1 group members into
  `produced` with no event; `ProductDriver::pull` emits only for the key it was
  asked for (`pull.rs:1974`).
- `ProductReadContext::publish_product` (`pull.rs:1671`) calls `memo.finish` with
  no telemetry at all. Callers: `jobs/runtime_demand.rs:482` (the demand cone's
  co-publication of every non-anchor member) and `jobs/artifact.rs:189`.

Measured on 00420_enum_take_drop_split, one compile: the log reports 3
`runtime_demand` settlements where at least 237 distinct RuntimeDemand products
settled -- 98.7% invisible.

This matters for hypothesis selection, not just precision: an undercount in a
known direction can make CHURN look like POPULATION. Do not start weighing the
three hypotheses below until fz-kdt.34.4 lands per-member settlement events.

## Signal (release compiler, 2026-08-24; re-confirmed at HEAD 2026-08-26)

enum_take_drop_split:

- 239 backend executables;
- 5,345 TransportShape settlements (floor);
- 5,037 CallableConstruction settlements (floor);
- about 110-115 ms attributed to those two product kinds.

enum_predicate_search:

- 209 backend executables;
- 2,390 TransportShape settlements (floor);
- 2,307 CallableConstruction settlements (floor);
- 366.994 ms compile session overall.

The old 242-executable / 2,625-callable numbers predate the closure-fanout
reduction and are stale.

## Three live hypotheses

1. Genuine population: distinct transport positions legitimately outnumber
   executables.
2. Churn: the same ProductKey settles repeatedly after displacement/reproduction.
3. Unit-cost scan: pending_strong_component enumerates pending/displaced
   candidates and calls dependency_reaches in both directions per candidate. The
   earlier fz-qe0 fix pruned settled nodes from those walks, but did not prove
   the remaining scan negligible.

Current public telemetry serializes ProductKey as kind only, so none can be
distinguished yet. fz-kdt.34 is the measurement prerequisite.

## Strategy

1. Count distinct ProductKeys versus total settlements, cache hits,
   displacements, and reproductions by kind.
2. Record recursive-group membership, candidate count, dependency-reach visits,
   and visits per product settlement.
3. Attribute product cost to semantic construction versus group discovery.
4. If population is genuine, trace the position inventory upstream and prove
   which semantic boundary owns each position.
5. If churn dominates, fix the earliest false generation/dependency movement.
6. If group scans dominate, replace repeated reachability queries with exact
   incrementally maintained cycle state; do not add a cache around a scan.
7. If more than one independent mechanism is proven, split implementation tickets
   then. Do not preserve three speculative concepts now.

## Acceptance

- Every product settlement is attributable to first production or exact
  dependency/generation movement.
- Distinct semantic positions map injectively to ProductKeys.
- Equal product reproduction preserves generation and wakes nobody.
- Recursive-group discovery performs work proportional to changed dependency
  edges, not candidate-set size times graph size.
- No full product inventory scan occurs per dependency read or product settlement.
- Repeated runs produce identical causal work multisets.
- Enum behavior remains byte-correct across interp, run, and build.
- Work-count regression tests replace wall-clock thresholds.

## Documentation

Update product/fact-engine and performance-instrumentation docs with the measured
mechanism and remove stale pre-fz-6gb counts.
title: Separate product population, re-settlement, and recursive-group scan cost
